WHY: acceptance is highly coupon-type-conditional; the trees must otherwise learn these ~5x2x5x3 grids from 8k rows and generalise poorly, while a smoothed target statistic (e.g. (sum_y + prior*k)/(n + k) with k~20) directly exposes the conditional mean with variance control. WHY: execution showed meta_gbdt/xgb/cb did not beat lgb_avg and cost ~500s; the OOF selection is itself noisy, so a rank-average of the two/three best decorrelated models with a coarsely tuned threshold (0.05 grid in [0.30,0.70]) is more robust and metric-faithful. HOW: in the fold loop pass eval_set and callbacks=[lgb.early_stopping(50, verbose=False)] for LGBM (and use best_iteration for refit n_estimators), keep `_tune_threshold` but shrink its grid, replace meta_gbdt candidate with rank-mean of available valid OOF columns, and keep candidates {lgb_avg, rank_vote, best_single}. Preserve loaders, make_stratified_folds, bundle keys (lgb_models/xgb_models/cb_models/threshold/label_map/use_stack, plus new 'selected'/'mode' fields), the argparse CLI, row_id/prediction output and fresh-process reload (predict must only load and inverse-map labels)."}}
message.reasoning_content:
The plateau at ~0.764-0.767 across many attempts suggests the model isn't the bottleneck — it's likely feature representation and validation noise. The 5-fold GBDT stack keeps landing at ~0.764, well below the ~0.77 ceiling. Key insight: coupon acceptance is strongly driven by coupon-type-specific interactions (e.g., Bar coupon is rarely accepted, Coffee House more), and the current engineer already creates many but the ordinal/frequency approach may lose signal. Also the threshold tuning on OOF over-fits slightly.

A genuinely different approach: feature engineering at the level of the coupon-type-conditional target statistic is risky (leakage). Instead, add explicit per-coupon-type statistical target-rate features computed only on training folds (safe, leakage-free with per-fold fitting). That harnesses the strongest signal (coupon type acceptance rate varies hugely). Also could add per-venue-frequency-interaction target-encoding via smoothed mean.

Also XGBoost/CatBoost additions apparently cost time (500s) and regressed. Given 600s budget, better to focus on a single well-tuned LGBM + one orthogonal model and better features.

Let me choose: data_processing_and_feature_engineering (add safe target-encoding + interaction features) and training_evaluation (tune LGBM hyperparams, add early stopping/increase estimators, use rank-averaging of predictors). Two modules.

Actually per instructions best to be modest. Add target encoding computed fold-safely, and improve training with more estimators + early stopping on OOF.

I'll pick data_processing_and_feature_engineering and training_evaluation.
